# Bharat-Bot vs a standard sidewalk robot: batch evaluation

*Generated by `python sim/evaluate.py` on 2026-10-15: 200 seeded runs (seeds 0–199) per scenario and robot, with the same street and the same dogs, auto-rickshaw and thief for every robot on a given seed. 3800 runs took 4.7 min on 11 worker processes (13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1355U). Every number is a mean with its 95 % confidence interval in brackets: Wilson intervals for rates, Student-t for means. *n* is the number of runs a metric applies to when that isn't every run.*

This answers the research's top priority (`india-delivery-robots.md` §4, item 1): a steel-manned baseline-vs-adapted comparison over 100+ seeded episodes with confidence intervals and an ablation. The film's runs are single, fixed streets; here the street, the dogs, the auto-rickshaw and the thief are drawn at random from the ranges in §5 for every run.

## Summary

- **Full delivery: Bharat-Bot delivered on 92% [88–95] of 200 random streets.** The standard robot from the film managed 0% [0–2]; a steel-manned version with the most generous §5 specs, a siren-locked lid and predictive obstacle stopping managed 0% [0–2]. On the same streets Bharat-Bot is +92 pts [+89, +96] ahead of the film's robot and +92 pts [+89, +96] ahead of the steel-manned one.
- **How the standard robot fails on the full route:** ran into a dog 56%, drove into water over its wading limit 25%, stuck 18%, ran out of time in a stand-off with the dogs 1% (film's robot); ran out of time in a stand-off with the dogs 60%, drove into water over its wading limit 28%, ran into a dog 10%, stuck <1% (steel-manned). It can't see holes or judge water depth, and with no dog policy a pack either gets run into or never loses interest.
- **One hazard at a time** (success for the film's robot / steel-manned / Bharat-Bot): pothole stretch 58% [51–65] / 68% [62–75] / 92% [88–95]; dog pack 0% [0–2] / 0% [0–2] / 100% [98–100]; theft attempt 0% [0–2] / 100% [98–100] / 98% [96–99]. A siren-locked lid is enough against the thief, which any robot can have; the dogs and the wet, broken road are where the India-specific design pays off.
- **Which adaptation matters most** (change in full-delivery success when it is removed): the dog freeze protocol −53 pts [−60, −46]; the tamper alarm −44 pts [−51, −37]; pothole & water perception −8 pts [−11, −4]; traffic yield −6 pts [−9, −2]; rocker-bogie (rigid chassis) 0 pts [0, 0]. The tamper alarm's weight depends on how often a thief shows up (half the streets here); per attempt, theft success goes from 0% [0–4] with the alarm to 99% [94–100] without it. The rocker-bogie never decided a run here: with perception it isn't needed, and without perception it only spares a few runs (stuck 0% [0–2] without perception, 2% [1–4] without both), because §5's holes are mostly small and shallow next to its 18 cm climb.
- **Where Bharat-Bot still fails:** stopped at water it can't wade or avoid on 13 of 200 full delivery runs; drove into water over its wading limit on 1 of 200 full delivery runs; ran into a person on 1 of 200 full delivery runs; stopped at water it can't wade or avoid on 15 of 200 pothole stretch runs; ran into a person on 3 of 200 theft attempt runs. It is also far from hole-free: a wheel went over at least 3 cm of hole on 84% [78–88] of full deliveries (2.4 [2.2, 2.7] holes per 100 m against 3.9 [3.5, 4.4] for the blind standard robot), and its suspension, not its planner, is what makes that harmless. Details and seeds to replay are below.
- **Biggest caveat:** the dog result rests on the film's hypothesis that a still, silent robot makes a pack lose interest about five times faster than one that has merely stopped (§4 item 3: label it a hypothesis). If any still robot calmed dogs that well, the steel-manned robot would get past the pack in 21% [16–27] of runs instead of 0% [0–2]. No value here was measured on a real street.

## Results by scenario

Robots: **standard robot (as in the film)**: 9 cm wheels that climb 6 cm, wades 3 cm, lid locked but no alarm, no dog or traffic policy. **Steel-manned**: the same robot with the best case of §5 (climbs 12 cm, wades 5 cm), a siren on the lid and predictive obstacle stopping for dogs. **Bharat-Bot**: the film's India-adapted robot.

## Ablation: which adaptation matters most

The full delivery again, on the same streets with the same agents, with one Bharat-Bot feature removed. *Change* is the paired per-seed difference in success from the complete robot. Without the dog protocol it still stops for dogs the way the steel-manned robot does (predictive obstacle stopping) but has no calm mode and no slow pass; without the rocker-bogie it is a rigid chassis that climbs 10.7 cm; without perception it plans as if the road were smooth.

| Bharat-Bot … | Success | Change | Stuck | Into deep water | Ran into a dog | Theft per attempt | Traffic conflict | What goes wrong instead |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| complete | 92% [88–95] | — | 0% [0–2] | 0% [0–3] | 0% [0–2] | 0% [0–4] | 6% [4–11] | — |
| without pothole & water perception | 85% [79–89] | −8 pts [−11, −4] | 0% [0–2] | 14% [9–19] | 1% [0–3] | 0% [0–4] | 4% [2–8] | drove into water over its wading limit (+13% of runs) |
| without the dog freeze protocol | 40% [33–46] | −53 pts [−60, −46] | 0% [0–2] | 0% [0–3] | 18% [13–24] | 0% [0–6] | 7% [4–12] | ran out of time in a stand-off with the dogs (+38% of runs) |
| without the tamper alarm | 48% [42–55] | −44 pts [−51, −37] | 0% [0–2] | 0% [0–3] | 0% [0–2] | 99% [94–100] | 6% [4–11] | stolen (+44% of runs) |
| without traffic yield | 87% [82–91] | −6 pts [−9, −2] | 0% [0–2] | 0% [0–3] | 0% [0–2] | 0% [0–4] | 31% [25–37] | touched the auto-rickshaw (+6% of runs) |
| without rocker-bogie (rigid chassis) | 92% [88–95] | 0 pts [0, 0] | 0% [0–2] | 0% [0–3] | 0% [0–2] | 0% [0–4] | 6% [4–11] | none |
| without perception and rocker-bogie | 84% [78–88] | −9 pts [−13, −5] | 2% [1–4] | 14% [9–19] | 1% [0–3] | 0% [0–4] | 4% [2–8] | drove into water over its wading limit (+13% of runs) |

*What goes wrong instead* is the failure that grew most compared with the complete robot on the same streets. Without traffic yield the delivery rate changes by −6 pts [−9, −2] (the robot and the auto touch beside the cow), but the bigger effect is on traffic: a conflict on 31% [25–37] of the auto's passes against 6% [4–11].

## Where Bharat-Bot still fails

- **Full delivery, stopped at water it can't wade or avoid:** 13 of 200 runs, e.g. 9.53 cm of water across its path at x = 42 m, 15.3 mm over its 8 cm limit. Replay with `python sim/simulate.py bharat_full --robot bharat` and `--seed 29`, `--seed 31`, `--seed 40`.
- **Full delivery, ran into a person:** 1 of 200 runs, e.g. drove into a person at 1.0 m/s. Replay with `python sim/simulate.py bharat_full --robot bharat` and `--seed 34`.
- **Full delivery, drove into water over its wading limit:** 1 of 200 runs, e.g. wheels in 8.00 cm of water, 0.01 mm over its 8 cm rating. Replay with `python sim/simulate.py bharat_full --robot bharat` and `--seed 88`.
- **Pothole stretch, stopped at water it can't wade or avoid:** 15 of 200 runs, e.g. 8.01 cm of water across its path at x = 7 m, 0.1 mm over its 8 cm limit. Replay with `python sim/simulate.py baseline_pothole --robot bharat` and `--seed 4`, `--seed 7`, `--seed 29`.
- **Dog pack:** no failures in 200 runs.
- **Theft attempt, ran into a person:** 3 of 200 runs, e.g. drove into a person at 1.0 m/s. Replay with `python sim/simulate.py baseline_theft --robot bharat` and `--seed 34`, `--seed 83`, `--seed 150`.
- **Holes it doesn't avoid (not a failure):** on 84% [78–88] of full deliveries a wheel went over at least 3 cm of hole, 2.4 [2.2, 2.7] per 100 m against 3.9 [3.5, 4.4] for the blind standard robot; on the 12 m pothole stretch it was 3.8 [3.1, 4.6] against 3.8 [2.8, 4.8], no better. Of the holes it drove over on the full route, 41% held water it waded on purpose (below its 8 cm limit), 26% were dry holes under 45 cm long that fall between its planner's sample points (every 0.5 m along the road, every 0.18-0.22 m across its footprint), and 33% were larger dry holes it clipped or couldn't steer round (the planner checks ±0.36 m either side but the wheels reach ±0.39 m, and the planned line is smoothed afterwards). The rocker-bogie climbs 18 cm, so none of them stopped it; a finer planning grid and a wider margin would keep its wheels out of most of them.
- **Traffic:** Bharat-Bot only yields to traffic before the cow; when it swerves into the lane round a pothole it doesn't check behind, so it forced the auto-rickshaw to brake or pass close on 6% [4–11] (n=193) of the runs where the auto came by.

What these mean: *drove into water over its wading limit* means its wheels went into water deeper than 8 cm; *ran into a person* is someone crossing its path inside its stopping distance (0.9 m from 1.6 m/s, braking at 1.4 m/s²); it stops for people in its path but doesn't predict where they walk; *stopped at water it can't wade or avoid* is the intended safe refusal: water deeper than its 8 cm wading limit covers every line through the lane, so it stops 1 m short and calls an operator.

## Rules of a seeded run

The film's runs only show what happens; a seeded run also scores it. Differences from the film's rules (all in `simulate.py`, none of them active without a seed):

- **Success** = the parcel handed over at the gate (full delivery) or the end of the stretch reached, within a time budget of the route at 0.5 m/s plus 30 s of waiting, with no failure on the way.
- **Run-ending failures:** stuck (the front wheels face a rise taller than the robot can climb; the film only checked the robot without pothole sensing, now every robot is checked); a wheel in water deeper than the robot's wading limit; stopped at water it can't wade or avoid (robots that see water refuse rather than wade in); stolen; footprints touching the auto-rickshaw.
- **Failures that don't end the run:** running into a dog or a person, i.e. footprints touching while the robot moves, the other is in front of it and the robot closes the gap at least as fast as they do. A dog or a person walking into a robot isn't counted against it.
- **Every robot plans its own lane** with the film's lattice planner (the film's standard robot drives a fixed straight line); robots that can't see potholes plan as if the road were smooth.
- **The auto-rickshaw driver isn't blind:** the film's auto follows a fixed line (in the film run its body overlaps the waiting robot by about 0.4 m). Here the driver moves right to pass the robot with 0.35 m to spare, using at most 0.5 m of the oncoming lane, and brakes behind it when there's no room. A *traffic conflict* is the robot forcing the auto to brake by more than 1 m/s or a pass closer than 0.2 m. The auto always turns in at least its stopping-sight distance behind the robot.
- **Dogs** keep the film's pack model (alert as a pack, chase to fixed spots around the robot, interest fades when the robot is still and silent) with §5's notice distance, chase speed and give-up time.
- **Metrics:** closest gaps are footprint to footprint (dogs 0.8 × 0.3 m, people 0.5 m discs, the auto 2.66 × 1.30 m), to dogs and people while the robot moves, to the auto at all times. Dog-chase duration is the time any dog is in chase mode, counted to the end of the run.

## Limits

- These are simulated streets. The ranges come from §5, but most of §5's dog, theft and pothole numbers are themselves estimates; no value was measured on a real Indian street (§4 item 2).
- The agents are simple and deterministic given their parameters: dogs never bite, a thief always flees a siren (so 0 % theft for alarmed robots is an upper bound on the alarm's effect), there is one dog pack, one cow, one vehicle and no crowd, and nobody reacts to the robot except the auto driver.
- The dog-protocol advantage leans on the calm-mode hypothesis above; the robot-vs-dog behaviour has never been tested (research §1.5).
- Physics is kinematic: no wheel slip, tipping, battery, heat or sensor noise. Perception is perfect for robots that have it (they see every hole and know every water depth); the standard robot sees none.
- Confidence intervals cover the randomness of the streets, not the uncertainty in the model.
